title: Getting started with Internet & SaaS: recommended provisioning and forwarding methods, deployment options and editing conventions

prose.label: Provisioning and authentication.
prose.text: {{provisioning-vs-authentication}} {{recommend-saml-scim}} The provisioning methods page words the same recommendation in [[zia.ad-integration.provisioning-methods:recommendation]].

prose.label: Logging.
prose.text: {{nss-via-vm}} Cloud NSS, which has no on-premises connectors, is in [[shared.nss.delivery-modes]].

provisioning-vs-authentication.statement: The configuration guide says users must be provisioned and authenticated to implement group and user policies and granular reporting; provisioning uploads usernames, groups and departments to the service database, and authentication lets the service identify traffic to enforce department, group and user policies and log by user and department.

quotes: To implement group and user policies and to leverage the granular reporting capabilities of the service, you must provision users and enable the Zscaler service to authenticate them.
Provisioning involves uploading usernames, groups, and departments to the service database.

Enabling authentication allows the Zscaler service to identify the traffic that it receives so it can enforce the configured department, group, and user policies, and provide user and department logging and reporting.

recommend-saml-scim.statement: Of the available provisioning and authentication methods, Zscaler recommends SAML for authentication and SCIM for provisioning.

quotes: Of the available methods, Zscaler recommends you use SAML for authentication and SCIM for provisioning.

forward-all-traffic.statement: Zscaler recommends that organizations forward all internet traffic, for all protocols and all destination ports, to the Zscaler service.

quotes: Zscaler recommends that organizations forward all internet traffic (traffic for all protocols and destined for all ports) to the Zscaler service so they can secure your internet traffic and apply policies accordingly.

gre-and-locations.statement: The guide says there are 4 preferred ways to forward traffic, calls a GRE tunnel ideal for forwarding internet-bound traffic from the corporate network, and says configuring locations is a requirement for GRE tunnels.

quotes: There are 4 preferred ways to forward your traffic:
A Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) tunnel is ideal for forwarding internet-bound traffic from your corporate network to the Zscaler service.
Configuring locations is a requirement for GRE tunnels.

pac-combination.statement: When PAC files forward traffic to the Zscaler service, Zscaler recommends using them in combination with tunneling, Surrogate IP and Zscaler Client Connector.

quotes: When using PAC files to forward traffic to the Zscaler service, Zscaler recommends that organizations use them in combination with tunneling, Surrogate IP, and Zscaler Client Connector.

private-virtual-edges.statement: The guide says forwarding to Public Service Edges is not always the right choice for some portions of an organization, which can instead forward to Private Service Edges or Virtual Service Edges for Internet & SaaS.

quotes: Sometimes, forwarding your traffic to Public Service Edges for Internet & SaaS is not the right choice for some portions of your organization.
you can choose to instead forward it to Private Service Edges or Virtual Service Edges for Internet & SaaS.

nss-via-vm.statement: The guide describes the Nanolog Streaming Service, without scoping it to a feed kind, as using a virtual machine to stream traffic logs in real time from the Zscaler NSS to a SIEM such as Splunk or ArcSight.

quotes: You can also utilize the Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS).
This uses a virtual machine (VM) to stream traffic logs in real-time from the Zscaler NSS to your security information and event management (SIEM) system, such as Splunk or ArcSight

data-center-count.statement: The What is Zscaler Internet & SaaS? page says the Zscaler ZTE is the world's largest security cloud with over 150 data centers, and the Traffic Forwarding reference architecture says ZIA is available in 150+ data centers.

quotes: Global Scalability: The Zscaler ZTE is the world’s largest security cloud, with over 150 data centers globally, providing high availability and localized peering.
ZIA is available in 150+ data centers around the world.

deployment-options.statement: The What is Zscaler Internet & SaaS? page lists these ways to connect traffic: Zscaler Client Connector, Cloud Tunnels (GRE or IPSec tunnels from branch office routers or SD-WAN gateways) and PAC files.

quotes: Organizations can easily connect their traffic to Internet & SaaS using several methods:
Zscaler Client Connector: A lightweight app installed on user devices that automatically tunnels traffic to the nearest Zscaler node.
Cloud Tunnels: Secure GRE or IPSec tunnels from branch office routers or SD-WAN gateways.
Proxy Auto-Configuration (PAC) Files: Lightweight files that instruct browsers to route traffic to the Zscaler service.

duplicate-rule.statement: A duplicated policy rule is identical to the original except for the Rule Order value, which shows the next available rule order; duplicating (cloning) DLP dictionaries is a different process.

quotes: If you duplicate a rule, the newly created rule is identical to the existing one, with the exception of the value in the Rule Order field.
The new rule shows the next available rule order value.
The process for duplicating (cloning) DLP dictionaries is different.

delete-confirm.statement: Some items are deleted with the Delete icon, which opens a confirmation window where CONFIRM must be typed before clicking Delete.

quotes: Some items can be deleted by clicking an icon.
Enter CONFIRM in the confirmation window that appears and then click Delete.
